name: Sea Glass Loupe
note: A liquid-glass loupe over live DOM: the clone underneath is magnified with a plain transform so text stays sharp, and only the bezel is bent by feDisplacementMap, fed a map computed from the capsule's signed distance field and run three times at slightly different scales for chromatic fringing. A spring drives the lens, and its velocity squashes the glass while the clone is counter-scaled so the content never smears.

name: Lido Ripple Pool
note: Hugo Elias' two-buffer wave equation on a coarse grid; each frame its gradient becomes a refraction offset and specular glint and its Laplacian a caustic gain, bilinearly upsampled to sample a mosaic floor painted once per size. Rain, pointer wakes and keyboard pebbles all inject the same cosine bump.

name: Fogged Tram Window
note: Condensation as an alpha mask: a soft brush stamped with destination-out wipes it, and a blotchy seed drawn back in every frame lets the fog creep home from the cold edges. The fogged layer is the same street pre-blurred, milked and grained once per size; beads run with stick-slip motion, wipe their own streaks, and each one clips a fisheye of the street drawn upside down.

name: Textured Glass Sampler
note: Six real glass patterns as SVG filters over a clone of the room: reeded and fluted glass are one cylindrical-lens tile repeated by feTile into a displacement map with its own shading, hammered and rain glass are stretched feTurbulence that also feeds feSpecularLighting from a pointer-tracked point light, and satin is fine noise, blur and a milk matrix. The panel slides like a door, and a new pattern wipes in with a WAAPI clip-path.

name: Soap Film Interference
note: Thin-film interference from first principles: reflectance 4R0 sin²(2πnd/λ) for a water film is integrated against an analytic fit of the CIE 1931 observer into a sRGB thickness LUT. The thickness field drains from the top, slides down as h², swirls on a divergence-free curl-noise flow and takes the pointer's breath; when the top reaches black film it pops, and the readout names the order and colour under the cursor.

name: Honey Jar Viscosity
note: Clavet-style viscoelastic SPH (2005) with 400 particles in the jar's own frame: pairwise viscosity impulses clamped so they can never reverse an approach, double density relaxation for near and far pressure, and wall friction so cold honey clings to the glass. Temperature drives viscosity through an exponential fit for honey; the surface is a metaball field shaded by its own gradient for the meniscus glint.

name: Ferrofluid Spikes
note: The Rosensweig instability side on: a short-solenoid field law sets the flux at every point of the surface, and only where it beats the critical field does the puddle break into cones at the capillary spacing. Each cone is a damped spring with concave quadratic flanks and a lean toward the pole, drawn in two rows for depth with softbox glints; get close and the centre cone leaps the gap.

name: Liquid Swipe Onboarding
note: The incoming slide is real DOM clipped by a path() whose edge is a cosine bell; four sprung numbers (bell centre, horizontal and vertical radius, and a solid band growing from the edge) are rebuilt into the path every frame. Pull past the threshold or flick and the band floods the card; let go early and the bell springs home. The chevron rides the crest, and the bell breathes at rest.
